format: Studio / Custom events: leader/follower role flexibility
requirement: DanceFlow policy (not a body rule): a couple-style entry needs exactly one leader and one follower (any people); the dance role is stored per participant per entry (dance_role: leader | follower); relationship role (student, professional, ...) is a separate dimension; Studio Country division schemes use only skill-level and age-group axes. No gender is collected or inferred, and no role-lock is enforced. Preserved unchanged by OD-27 Option B for initial activation.
enforcement_point: participantShapeErrors in src/lib/competition/participantRoles.ts and its SQL mirror _comp10c4_participant_shape_errors; division schemes in src/lib/competition/setup/studioCustomV3.ts.

tests.name: couple-style formats need exactly one leader and one follower

interpretation_notes: Approved behavior and tested as written (the 10C.4 migration header states the intent: NDCA treats every couple as a leader plus a follower regardless of gender), but: (a) the role is per entry, so nothing checks that the same partnership keeps its roles across different entries or Dance Categories; (b) the studioCustomV3 scheme note cites UCWDC II.A.7 yet models only skill level and age group, not the Mixed-Role dimension that II.A.7 names; (c) no user-facing disclosure exists; (d) tests were not run for this docs-only entry; (e) the client and profile tables were not audited for gender fields. Not any body's rule.
decision_refs: OD-27 (owner decision 2026-11-23: Option B retain Studio/Custom role flexibility; document body limitations; retrospective audit PR #795)
